4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 的回答；随后把 prompt 与生成段重组为完整序列做 teacher-forcing 二次前向，取最后一层隐状态、切片对准生成段，交 `get_query_tokens_eval` 全局搜索指称区间得到分割查询。单轮 QA 独立成对话、按三级键写入预测 JSON；多轮为 LLaVA 式滚动历史，点 token 与图像仅第 0 轮注入，记录带 `turn_idx`。推理不做 FPS 聚合；`save_pred_qa_dir` 须显式开启否则写盘报错；JSON 先于分割解码写出且与 mIoU 通道独立；回答保留特殊标记供文本指标，无 `

` 时查询退化为零向量、其 mask 被置为 1e-4。 ### u4-l6 2D 图像分支：Joint 与 3D-only 两种变体 本讲拆解 Ground3D-LMM 的 2D 图像分支两种变体。Joint 变体除点云 token 外，通过 Qwen-VL 原生 message 里的 image 条目注入一帧 RGB 图像，max_pixels 与 min_pixels 经智能缩放把像素钳在固定区间，封顶视觉 token 预算；图像与点 token 策略一致，只在首条 user 消息注入一次。3D-only 无独立代码分支：image_dir 为 None 时 image 条目变 image=None，由 _prepare_messages_data 统一过滤，序列零视觉 token，两变体共享全部解码代码。配置仅差三字段 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir；LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 失配会被 strict=False 静默吞掉，模型无声退回基座 Qwen，是重大隐患。训练解码器 Grounded_Decoder_Joint 恒有图，按场景名在双图像目录分流。抽帧工具链由 infos pkl 驱动，产出 image_dir 下的「场景/帧号.jpg」目录树，与解码器的路径拼接构成纯字符串契约。 ### u5-l1 Mask2Former 式查询解码器：逐层前向 本讲剖析查询解码器的逐层前向：共 6 层，每层由「Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN」三件套组成，均为后归一化残差结构、逐场景循环不拼批。核心结论：交叉注意力采用 Mask2Former 式 masked attention，查询只注意上一轮预测掩码内的超点（布尔 attn_mask 约定 True=禁止注意）；自注意力以 ~eye 掩码实现查询隔离，每条查询仅注意自身，防止不同指称目标互相干扰；_forward_head 用 einsum 点积对归一化查询与掩码特征动态打分，sigmoid 低于 0.5 处置为禁止、全禁止行被救援放行并 detach。训练路径把整场景 2560 维语言查询经 query_proj 桥降至 256 维后一次过 6 层，初始 head 加各层 head 共 7 份预测、5 份作辅助深监督；推理路径逐 QA 独立跑完整 6 层，零查询行掩码置 1e-4 哨兵标记无接地，取末层掩码上采样至点级。输出 masks、aux_outputs、original_queries 与 language_losses，交由下一讲损失函数消费。 ### u5-l2 损失函数：语言损失 + 分割损失 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 训练损失如何由预测变成可反传的标量。核心模块三个：Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合器是无可训练参数的纯组装者，把解码器预测、sp_gt_masks、language_losses 与 original_queries 分发给两个子损失器并合并字典，输出 text_seg_loss 与 cot_loss 两键，由 mmengine parse_losses 求和；语言与分割的相对权重只能调各子损失器的 loss_weight。CoTCriterion 语言损失是仅落在 assistant 回复 token 上的交叉熵（preprocess_chatml 把提问置 -100），先场景内平均、场景间再 macro-average。TextPrompt_Criterion_Glamm 分割损失对逐超点掩码做 BCE+Dice，依托「

数量契约」行对齐而无需匈牙利匹配；关键概念有有效行过滤（零向量查询且 GT 全 NaN 的行剔除，零查询判定必须在投影前的 original_queries 上做）、dice_scale=4 的 Dice 放大、fix_mean_loss 的无效场景补偿、五层 1/i 递减加权的辅助深监督。GT 侧 sp_gt_seg 逐 QA 生成后拼接为逐场景张量，与查询行、掩码行三方对齐。 ### u5-l3 训练配置与启动：train.sh 背后发生了什么 本讲把唯一训练配置归纳为「模型、数据、优化、起点、钩子」五问清单：数据侧用 ConcatDataset 把 ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 拼成一条训练流，两个子数据集仅差 data_root 与 ann_file，靠裸文件名契约共享同一 pipeline，并以 _delete_ 重建 dataset、显式关闭 val/test 防继承污染。启动链为 train.sh→dist_train.sh（探测空闲端口后经 torch.distributed.launch 起 4 进程）→tools/train.py→Runner.from_cfg→runner.train()，训练循环是 EpochBasedTrainLoop；--amp 只是把 OptimWrapper 换成 AmpOptimWrapper 壳。优化用 AdamW 加 PolyLR，paramwise_cfg 按参数名子串分层调学习率：'backbone' 是匹配不到任何参数的死键（主干属性名是 unet，实际以基准 lr 训练），'reason' 与 'decoder' 命中语言塔可训练参数（LoRA 与词嵌入两端）。load_from 非严格加载仅初始化 3D 稀疏主干，语言塔由 from_pretrained 独立加载、LoRA 随机起步；--resume 与 load_from 互斥且命令行优先，恢复完整训练状态。 ### u6-l1 分割指标 Part3DGlamm_SegMetric：mIoU 怎么算 本讲解读 `unified_metric.py` 中的 `get_iou` 函数与 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 指标类。核心结论：解码器输出超点级 logits，先 sigmoid 过 `sp_score_thr=0.4` 阈值，再经 `mask[:, superpoints]` 列索引广播成点级掩码；`qa_gt_masks` 与 `qa_pred_masks` 按轮 1:1 对齐，GT 行多则预测补零（诚实惩罚漏检）、行少则预测截断，无 GT 的预测条目仅供可视化。`get_iou` 做两级平均：QA 内先对有效 GT 行（行和大于 0）逐实例取 IoU 均值，再跨 QA 平均；无 `

` 标签任务（如 existence_verification）的 GT 是全 NaN 哨兵，NaN 行和判据自动剔除，无需任务名过滤。`process` 只存每场景 IoU 数组以省内存，`compute_metrics` 拼平后输出 QA Seg mIoU 及严格大于口径的 Precision_half/quarter；`min_num_points`、`id_offset` 等为抄自父类的死参数。 ### u6-l2 评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh 与配置族 本讲剖析统一评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh：它把「数据集 × QA 层级 × 子任务」三层循环展开成一串 tools/test.py 调用，经 --cfg-options 覆盖 QA_Generation_Test 的三级旋钮 task_level/task_type/sub_task 与预测输出目录，目录树本身就是按任务归档的结果。核心概念是 LoRA rank 探测（probe_lora_rank）：joint 变体 r=16、3D 变体 r=32，rank 与配置错配时权重被 strict=False 静默丢弃、模型无声退回基座 Qwen，auto 模式靠扫描 lora_A 的 shape[0] 在加载前自动选配置。评估配置族是 2×2 矩阵（scannet/scannetpp × joint/_3d），_3d 版仅覆盖 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir 三字段。三级过滤为严格匹配且失败不报错：--levels 非法值在 Bash 侧 LEVEL_MAP 即拦下，--sub_tasks 拼错则静默空跑，权威子任务清单是 ALL_TASKS，长评估前宜 DRYRUN 干跑核对。 ### u6-l3 文本指标：APE、δ@1.25、LLM judge 与 GM-δ 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 的文本评测工具 evaluate_text_metrics.py：它与 mIoU 独立，经 --stages 选择 ape、judge、gmdelta 三阶段。关键概念：任务感知的递归展平（flatten_with_task、gather_samples）把任意嵌套或多轮的预测 JSON 展平为带 _task 标签的扁平样本列表，标签按「meta_info.group → 最近包裹键 → 路径目录名」三级回退；ape 阶段先用文本 LLM 按任务形状抽取数字，再逐对计算 APE 与 δ@1.25，预测缺数被「罚 0」（APE=100%、δ=∞、成功=0），GT 为 0 的对跳过，任务内对 QA 宏观平均、overall 池化平均；judge 阶段用 Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct 对全部任务打 1-10 分，仅聚合幻觉与完整性两维，贪心解码保证可复现，clean_text 定义了但未接线；GM-δ 要求点级掩码 IoU>0.3 且该 QA 全部数值对 δ≤1.25 同时成立，文本与掩码两通道靠「目录镜像＋场景同名＋按位对齐」的纯字符串契约 join（掩码来自推理时 mask dump 落盘的 npy），须显式开启并提供 --mask_dump_dir。核心结论：能量化的数值误差用硬公式与 --selftest 单测覆盖，难量化的幻觉与完整性才交给 LLM 裁判。 ### u6-l4 接地可视化：导出彩色 PLY 点云 本讲打通「被 mIoU 指标丢弃的逐点掩码」到彩色点云的完整链路，覆盖 `predict()` 出口的 mask dump 旁路、离线工具 `export_grounding_ply.py` 与写入器 `grounding_viz.py` 三个模块。核心结论：dump 由环境变量 `MASK_DUMP_DIR` 或配置项 `save_viz_dir` 开启，环境变量优先；逐场景以 object 数组落盘预测与 GT 掩码，按场景名与同名点云 bin 配对；批量评估须用 `--mask-dump` 镜像目录树，防止同场景被子任务静默覆盖。导出分 combine 与 per_qa 两种模式，`--group N` 使颜色在每组内重新起算。染色规则：每个 dump 条目（一条 QA 或多轮的一轮）经行并集后至多占一个区域，单条 QA 内多个指称会被并成同色；颜色按五色调色板循环、重叠处先到先得；`max_frac` 双判据滤除空掩码与全 True 退化掩码（零查询哨兵经阈值所致）；背景乘 `dim_bg` 调暗后写出二进制 PLY。 ### u7-l1 迁移基准：ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 的微调评估 本讲把 Ground3D-LMM 迁移到 ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 两个外部基准，做逐数据集微调后评估（非零样本）。模块一：整场景转换链——共享基类以标注 JSON 的场景键为权威、复用 ScanNet 基座，外部 QA 以 qa_data 整段写入 pkl，v2 规范化借用 reason3d 例程（'scanrefer' 不是合法转换 key）；模块二：超点级 GT 生成——ScanRefer 为实例级指称分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_ins 的 object_id 行、答案回显描述原句，Reason3D 为语义级推理分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_sem 行、答案为类别名，GT 缺失以 NaN 整行占位；模块三：用 linspace 为每场景确定性抽取 20 张 RGB 视图；模块四：2×2 评估配置矩阵（数据集 × 3D/3D+2D），解码器拆为 Eval_Text 与 Eval_MultiImg，LoRA 统一 r=32，mIoU 基线 38.72/41.30/36.35/41.29，加入 2D 视图稳定涨点，证明架构不限于自建数据；复现需隔离四路输出目录、容忍约一点多方差。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u7-l2 - 文件名: u7-l2-extending-the-project.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u7-l2-extending-the-project.md - 标题: 二次开发：新增子任务、数据集与替换底座 - 学习阶段: advanced - 主题: 总结项目的扩展点：新增 QA 子任务、接入新数据集、更换/升级 LMM 底座（base_model 分支）、调整 LoRA 与点 token 预算。 - 学习目标: 列出新增子任务时数据、transform、评估三处的改动点；说明新增数据集需要实现的 Dataset/Transform/Converter；评估替换 LLM 底座（qwen2_5_vl 路径）的可行性 - 应覆盖的最小模块: 新增子任务的改动链，新增数据集的三件套，更换 LLM 底座（base_model 分支），LoRA/聚合器的调参入口 - 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

…

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build 构建三大组件——SpConvUNet 稀疏卷积主干、Grounded_Decoder_Joint 解码器（内含 Qwen3-VL）、Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合损失器；query_thr、set_query_mask、pred_iou 等是继承自 UniSeg3D 的死开关，故训练需 find_unused_parameters=True。loss() 用 superpoint_bias 累计偏移生成 batch_offsets，把各场景超点编号平铺进全局空间，extract_feat 先 scatter_mean 全局池化再按偏移切回逐场景，偏移仅存在于池化一步，GT sp_gt_seg 本就是场景局部故无需平移。predict() 与 loss 共用同段 3D 主干，差异在不传 elastic_coords、GT 保持逐 QA 列表、解码器走 infer_reason_eval 分支；qa_predict_by_feat 以 mask[:, superpoints] 把超点级预测与 GT 上采样到点级，按「有 GT 才对齐、不足补零、超出截断」对齐行数，产出 PointData(qa_pred_masks, qa_gt_masks) 供指标计算，并可经 MASK_DUMP_DIR 落盘 .npy 供可视化。 ### u3-l2 稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet 本讲讲解稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet（改编自 SPFormer）。点云经 collate 体素化（voxel_size=0.02）后构成 SparseConvTensor 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），稀疏卷积只对非空体素存储与计算。ResidualBlock 是 pre-norm 双 3×3 SubMConv3d 加恒等跳连：子流形卷积不改变活跃位置，故两支可按行相加；同层卷积共用 indice_key 复用索引规则。SpConvUNet 以递归表达五级 U 形（num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]），每级含 blocks、conv、u、deconv、blocks_tail 五件套，deconv 与 conv # 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。
```

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": "Ground3D-LMM 是一个基于 OpenMMLab（mmdet3d/mmengine）框架的 3D 点云接地大模型项目，由三大部分组成：SpConvUNet 稀疏点云编码器、注入点云 token 的 Qwen3-VL-4B（LoRA 微调）、Mask2Former 式 6 层查询解码器，配合 247 万 QA 对的 Ground3D 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build 构建三大组件——SpConvUNet 稀疏卷积主干、Grounded_Decoder_Joint 解码器（内含 Qwen3-VL）、Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合损失器；query_thr、set_query_mask、pred_iou 等是继承自 UniSeg3D 的死开关，故训练需 find_unused_parameters=True。loss() 用 superpoint_bias 累计偏移生成 batch_offsets，把各场景超点编号平铺进全局空间，extract_feat 先 scatter_mean 全局池化再按偏移切回逐场景，偏移仅存在于池化一步，GT sp_gt_seg 本就是场景局部故无需平移。predict() 与 loss 共用同段 3D 主干，差异在不传 elastic_coords、GT 保持逐 QA 列表、解码器走 infer_reason_eval 分支；qa_predict_by_feat 以 mask[:, superpoints] 把超点级预测与 GT 上采样到点级，按「有 GT 才对齐、不足补零、超出截断」对齐行数，产出 PointData(qa_pred_masks, qa_gt_masks) 供指标计算，并可经 MASK_DUMP_DIR 落盘 .npy 供可视化。 ### u3-l2 稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet 本讲讲解稀疏卷积主干 SpConvUNet（改编自 SPFormer）。点云经 collate 体素化（voxel_size=0.02）后构成 SparseConvTensor 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），稀疏卷积只对非空体素存储与计算。ResidualBlock 是 pre-norm 双 3×3 SubMConv3d 加恒等跳连：子流形卷积不改变活跃位置，故两支可按行相加；同层卷积共用 indice_key 复用索引规则。SpConvUNet 以递归表达五级 U 形（num_planes=[32,64,96,128,160]），每级含 blocks、conv、u、deconv、blocks_tail 五件套，deconv 与 conv # Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
import argparse
import sys
from os import path as osp

# Add data directory to path for imports
sys.path.insert(0, osp.join(osp.dirname(__file__), '..', 'data'))

from indoor_converter import create_indoor_info_file
from update_infos_to_v2 import update_pkl_infos


def scannet_data_prep(root_path, info_prefix, out_dir, workers):
    """Prepare the info file for scannet dataset.

    Args:
        root_path (str): Path of dataset root.
        info_prefix (str): The prefix of info filenames.
        out_dir (str): Output directory of the generated info file.
        workers (int): Number of threads to be used.
    """
    create_indoor_info_file(
        root_path, info_prefix, out_dir, workers=workers)
    info_train_path = osp.join(out_dir, f'{info_prefix}_oneformer3d_infos_train.pkl')
    info_val_path = osp.join(out_dir, f'{info_prefix}_oneformer3d_infos_val.pkl')
    info_test_path = osp.join(out_dir, f'{info_prefix}_oneformer3d_infos_test.pkl')
    update_pkl_infos(info_prefix, out_dir=out_dir, pkl_path=info_train_path)
    update_pkl_infos(info_prefix, out_dir=out_dir, pkl_path=info_val_path)
    update_pkl_infos(info_prefix, out_dir=out_dir, pkl_path=info_test_path)


def part3d_glamm_data_prep(root_path, info_prefix, out_dir, workers, qa_data_dir):
    """Prepare the info file for part3d_glamm dataset.

    Args:
        root_path (str): Path of dataset root.
        info_prefix (str): The prefix of info filenames.
        out_dir (str): Output directory of the generated info file.
        workers (int): Number of threads to be used.
    """
    # The converter lives alongside this script in tools/.
    sys.path.insert(0, osp.dirname(__file__))
    from part3d_glamm_data_utils import Part3DGlammData
    
    save_path = root_path if out_dir is None else out_dir
    
    # Generate infos for train, val, test splits

    train_filename = osp.join(save_path, f'{info_prefix}_infos_train.pkl')
    val_filename = osp.join(save_path, f'{info_prefix}_infos_val.pkl')
    # test_filename = osp.join(save_path, f'{info_prefix}_infos_test.pkl')
    
    train_dataset = Part3DGlammData(root_path=root_path, split='train', save_path=save_path, qa_data_dir=qa_data_dir)
    val_dataset = Part3DGlammData(root_path=root_path, split='val', save_path=save_path, qa_data_dir=qa_data_dir)
    # test_dataset = Part3DGlammData(root_path=root_path, split='test', save_path=save_path)
    
    import mmengine



    infos_train = train_dataset.get_infos(num_workers=workers, has_label=True)
    mmengine.dump(infos_train, train_filename, 'pkl')
    print(f'{info_prefix} info train file is saved to {train_filename}')
    update_pkl_infos(info_prefix, out_dir=out_dir, pkl_path=train_filename)
    
    infos_val = val_dataset.get_infos(num_workers=workers, has_label=True)
    mmengine.dump(infos_val, val_filename, 'pkl')
    print(f'{info_prefix} info val file is saved to {val_filename}')
    update_pkl_infos(info_prefix, out_dir=out_dir, pkl_path=val_filename)

    
    # infos_test = test_dataset.get_infos(num_workers=workers, has_label=False)
    # mmengine.dump(infos_test, test_filename, 'pkl')
    # print(f'{info_prefix} info test file is saved to {test_filename}')
    
    # Update to v2 format
    
    


parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Data converter arg parser')
parser.add_argument('--dataset', default='part3d_glamm', help='name of the dataset')
parser.add_argument(
    '--root-path',
    type=str,
    default='data/scannet',
    help='specify the root path of dataset')
parser.add_argument(
    '--out-dir',
    type=str,
    default='data/scannet/',
    required=False,
    help='name of info pkl')

parser.add_argument(
    '--qa_data_dir',
    type=str,
    default='data/scannet/refined_qa_data',
    required=False,
    help='name of info pkl')

parser.add_argument('--extra-tag', type=str, default='part3d_glamm')
parser.add_argument(
    '--workers', type=int, default=4, help='number of threads to be used')
args = parser.parse_args()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    from mmdet3d.utils import register_all_modules
    register_all_modules()

    if args.dataset in ('scannet', 'scannet200'):
        scannet_data_prep(
            root_path=args.root_path,
            info_prefix=args.extra_tag,
            out_dir=args.out_dir,
            workers=args.workers)
    elif args.dataset == 'part3d_glamm':
        part3d_glamm_data_prep(
            root_path=args.root_path,
            info_prefix=args.extra_tag,
            out_dir=args.out_dir,
            workers=args.workers,
            qa_data_dir=args.qa_data_dir)
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError(f'Don\'t support {args.dataset} dataset.')

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

schema.name: Glob
schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime.
